we have measured the temperature, pressure, density, and entropy profiles for the SPT cluster sample and that the profiles are similar to those measured at z ~ 0.

we have measured the redshift evolution of the average temperature profile in 80 SPT galaxy clusters and find that the pressure profile outside the core evolves little with redshift, and the entropy profile at 0.7 R_(500) evolves little with red-shift, but the entropy profile at R_(500) shows a slight flattening at high redshift.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, at the current level of precision, the pressure and entropy profiles of galaxy clusters appear to be self-similar and show no significant evolution with redshift out to z ~ 1.

the average pressure profiles of clusters are remarkably self-similar across a wide range in redshift, while the average temperature profiles are not, reflecting the redshift dependence of the cluster mass function.
